title: Where can you fly direct from Cork Airport?
author: Brogan
intro: Cork flies to around 35 destinations in winter, mostly in Spain, Portugal, the UK and big European cities. Ryanair and Aer Lingus fly most routes, KLM and Air France connect you to the world, and Ryanair adds Alicante this winter. Here's what flies and how to choose.
seo_title: Where can you fly direct from Cork? (2026 guide)
seo_description: Ryanair and Aer Lingus fly most routes from Cork, with sun in Spain and Portugal, city breaks and KLM to Amsterdam. No direct long-haul. Checked Nov 2026.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Main airlines:** Ryanair and Aer Lingus
- **Winter routes:** about 35 last winter
- **New this winter:** Ryanair to Alicante
- **Long-haul:** none direct yet

We checked these routes in November 2026. Routes and days of the week change every season, so check the airline's timetable or the airport's flight schedule before you plan a trip around one.

sections.heading: Who flies from Cork
sections.text:
Ryanair flies the most routes from Cork, about 22 last winter, mainly to sun spots and cities in Spain, Portugal, Poland and the UK. Aer Lingus flies to the UK, Spain, Portugal and a growing list of European cities.

For anywhere further, the useful routes are the hubs. KLM flies to Amsterdam three times a day, and Air France added flights to Paris Charles de Gaulle last winter, so you can connect to North America, Asia and Africa on one ticket.

sections.heading: Winter routes worth knowing
sections.text:
| Destination | Airline | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) | Ryanair, Aer Lingus | the Costa del Sol and winter sun |
| Faro, for the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve) | Ryanair, Aer Lingus | golf, walking and mild winters |
| Alicante | Ryanair | new this winter, twice a week |
| [Seville](/destinations/seville) | Ryanair | a warm winter city break |
| [Prague](/destinations/prague) | Aer Lingus | now flying all year |
| [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) | KLM | three a day, connections worldwide |

Last winter Aer Lingus also flew to Geneva for the ski season, on Saturdays from late December, and the Canaries have been a regular part of Cork's winter schedule. Check whether they're flying on your dates.

sections.heading: Winter sun
sections.text:
For warmth in December to February, [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) and the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve) are the easiest choices, with highs of about 16 to 18°C. That's good weather for walking, golf and long lunches outside, but not reliably beach weather.

For proper beach warmth, the Canaries are the safest bet, at about 20 to 22°C. If there's no direct flight to the island you want on your dates, check Dublin, which has more choice, or connect through a Spanish airport.

Tip: on routes that only fly two or three times a week, check the flight days before you book a hotel, so the trip length works.

sections.heading: City breaks
sections.text:
Cork's city-break choice has grown. Aer Lingus now flies to [Prague](/destinations/prague) all year, and summer 2026 added Nice and Santiago de Compostela. KLM's [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) flights make an easy weekend, and Ryanair flies to cities in Poland and the UK.

For a winter weekend, [Seville](/destinations/seville) is one of the warmest city breaks in Europe, at about 16°C by day in January. Prague is better for Christmas markets and cosy pubs.

sections.heading: Long-haul and connections
sections.text:
There are no regular direct long-haul flights from Cork. The airport has said it wants routes to Boston, New York and Toronto as it grows, but none had been announced when we checked. For now, most people:

- **Connect through Amsterdam or Paris** with KLM or Air France, on one ticket.
- **Fly from Dublin**, about two and a half hours by road, which has the most direct flights to North America.
- **Fly from Shannon**, which has summer flights to the US.

Watch out: both Dublin and Shannon have US preclearance, so you clear US immigration before you board. Allow at least three hours at the airport, and have your ESTA sorted before you leave home. Our guide to [how early to arrive at Shannon](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-shannon-airport) explains how it works.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Cork?
sections.text:
For winter sun, try [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) or the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve). For a city break, look at [Prague](/destinations/prague), [Seville](/destinations/seville) or [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam). The [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) pages have more ideas, and our guide to [how early to arrive at Cork Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-cork-airport) covers the airport itself.

If your family can't agree, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or add a few ideas to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Which airlines fly from Cork Airport?
faqs.answer: Mainly Ryanair and Aer Lingus. KLM flies to Amsterdam and Air France to Paris, which are useful for connections further afield.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct from Cork to America?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Cork has no regular direct US flights. Most people connect through Amsterdam or Paris, or fly from Dublin or Shannon.

faqs.question: Can you fly from Cork to Alicante?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ryanair has added a twice-weekly Cork to Alicante route for winter 2026/27.

faqs.question: Does Aer Lingus fly from Cork to Prague?
faqs.answer: Yes. Aer Lingus started flying from Cork to Prague in October 2025, and the route now runs all year.
